title: Close Update: Trade Issues Keep Dow Defensive But Major Averages Close Month With a Bang
text:
Close Update: Trade Issues Keep Dow Defensive But Major Averages Close Month With a Bang August 31, 2018, 04:34:56 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
U.S stocks were mixed at Friday's close with the Dow Jones Industrial Average lower for a second day as lingering fears of a trade war with China coupled with protracted negotiations with Canada lured investors to safe havens. The S&P 500 was slightly higher while the Nasdaq held a modest gain with the help of Apple ( AAPL ), Cisco ( CSCO ) and Ulta ( ULTA ).
At the close of the week and the month, all three indices closed higher with the Dow up 1.0% for the week and up 2.1% from July. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both extended their monthly winning streak for a fifth month with a gain of 3.0% and 5.7%, respectively. For the week, the S&P 500 was higher by 0.9% and the Nasdaq by 2.1%.
Wall Street remained defensive from Thursday's late sell-off triggered by President Donald Trump's support of additional tariffs on Chinese imports. Losses reverberated throughout emerging markets as worries a trade war between the world's two largest economies will devastate vulnerable economies left the Indonesia rupiah at its lowest level in 20 years.
Losses accelerated in the U.S. after trade talks with Canada stalled. Although negotiations will continue next week, Canadian foreign minister left little doubt as to the lack of progress by her remarks to reporters earlier Friday which left the Dow with a triple-digit loss.
The fallout from U.S. trade sanctions against China prompted Ford ( F ) to shelve its plans to import the Chinese-made Focus. Shares of the carmaker fell more than 2%, weighing down the entire auto sector.
Data released this morning was mixed. The Chicago purchasing manager's index dipped to 63.6 in August from 65.5 previously, although production and new orders continued to accelerate.
The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey improved to 96.2 in August from 95.3 initially, but components were soft suggesting consumers are trimming their spending due to higher interest rates and market prices.
